title: Per-era coverage report
description: One row of data/curated/era-coverage.jsonl for every era the era table (tools/dataset/rules/game-eras.json) declares for team statistics, in the table's own order: the same aggregation of per-game coverage markers as event-coverage.jsonl, but keyed by the era the game was played in (spec D4, R6). Every declared era is present, including the ones no game has reached yet — an absent row would be indistinguishable from 'nobody looked', the distinction event-games.jsonl makes for events. Because a game carries exactly one era, the `games` column sums to the number of rows in games.jsonl, and each group's counts sum to `games`; the invariant gate re-counts both. The window boundaries are the table's, never inferred from the corpus; `from` repeats the boundary so a reader can sort and read this file alone.

era.description: The era id, as games.jsonl states it in `era`.

from.description: First UTC date this era governs, copied from the era table.

games.description: How many emitted games carry this era. Sums across rows to the number of games in games.jsonl.

events.description: How many distinct events contribute at least one game to this era.

coverage.description: The three field groups a game's coverage marker names, aggregated over the games in this era.

state.description: `complete` only when every game in the era is, `unavailable` when the era has no games, `partial` otherwise.
